messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER -> gpu-17 (us-west-2) repeating driver resets (Xid 13) + ECC correctable spike. Multiple inference pods restarted; some containers OOM'd during kvcache warmup. Auto-evac triggered but some jobs retried and hit repeated failures. Please triage. link: https://internal.redwood/sys/incidents/3849998765
Rita SRE: I'm on it. grabbing logs now. Can someone confirm whether this is isolated to gpu-17 or a node-group pattern?
Tom Eng-runtime: looking at telemetry — gpu-17 shows a burst of correctable ECC (cc_errors ~ 120 in 10m) and then repeated Xid 13. Driver reports "GPU HANG" followed by nv-host-reset. Not seeing the same signature on other nodes in the rack.
Jordan Ops: cordoning gpu-17 now to prevent new pods: `kubectl cordon gpu-17-usw2`
Rita SRE: thanks. Start draining non-critical pods and keep serving-critical pinned? We should avoid evicting long-running customer bridges until we have fallback route.
Lina Support: @Rita SRE we have two customers showing increased error rates in the dashboard (cust-a, cust-c). Cust-a teams were notified automatically. Do we want a customer bridge? :thinking_face:
Maya MLOps: I'd prefer we open a bridge if this affects model serving latency >20% for them. For now we can route their traffic to the quantized variant (q4_0) in the same region — that reduces memory pressure.
Chris Oncall: draining in progress. Command used: ```kubectl drain gpu-17-usw2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m```  evictions 14/18 so far. Noticing kubelet reports OOMKills on `inference-worker-xyz` during eviction.
Tom Eng-runtime: OOMKills are happening during kvcache restore. Kernel dmesg snippet: ```[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 13, pid=2314, GPU has fallen off the bus``````[ 12346.000002] EDAC mc0: ECC errors corrected: 47``` Looks like ECC correctables correlate with Xid surfacing.
Rita SRE: decision: full evacuation of gpu-17 to avoid cascade. We'll cordon+drain and reboot node from BMC after drains complete. Also escalate to infra for hardware trace: @Jordan Ops can you file an HCI ticket and request a forced power cycle?
Jordan Ops: HCI ticket created (#HCI-94821). Scheduling immediate reboot; hardware tech on call. ETA 12m.
Maya MLOps: while we evacuate, apply runtime fallback for affected model routes: reduce batch_size from 8 -> 4 and enable prefix cache hot-path disabled to reduce KV memory. Config snippet: ```service.routes['/v1/generate'].batch_size=4
service.runtime.kvcache.enabled=false```
Lina Support: opening customer bridge now and adding notes. customer-bridge-bot: Created bridge: https://meet.redwood/bridges/3849998765 (bridge id 3849998765). Inviting cust-a and cust-c.
customer-bridge-bot: Auto-post: Incident severity set to P1 (potential customer impact). Notifying on-call escalation policy.
Tom Eng-runtime: quick mitigation — add fallback routing to q4_0 for spikes: `routing.apply --from model-x --to model-x-q4_0 --threshold 5%` This will divert only a % of traffic to the cheaper quantized variant to keep latency SLOs.
Chris Oncall: kube drain completed. All critical serving pods relocated. Reboot job queued at BMC.
Rita SRE: good. Post-reboot, we'll run memtest and nvcheck tools. Also gather nv_driver debug logs before reprovision. Jordan, capture `nvidia-smi -q -x` and full dmesg dump pre-reboot.
Jordan Ops: captured and uploaded to artifacts: s3://infra-artifacts/incidents/3849998765/gpu-17-logs.tar.gz
Tom Eng-runtime: note for follow-ups — we saw a repeating pattern: small ECC correctable bursts lead to Xid 13 then driver reset. Hypothesis: thermal transient + marginal DIM could be amplifying soft errors during high kvcache load. Adding hardware and daemon telemetry to postmortem.
Lina Support: customers onboarded to bridge. Cust-a rep reports ~20% increase in API errors around 10:03 UTC. We'll keep them updated every 15m.
Rita SRE: next actions: 1) wait for BMC reboot, 2) run diagnostics, 3) if hardware looks flaky, mark node for replacement and migrate remaining capacity, 4) run intermittent soak tests on restored node before returning to production.
Maya MLOps: also recommend adding a short-term runtime guard: fail-open to smaller context size for affected model families to reduce working set. Will PR config to runtime repo now.
Tom Eng-runtime: creating short-lived alert rule to catch ECC rate > 50/min and auto-shed low-priority batches to avoid OOM cascades. Patch: https://git.redwood/runtime/changesets/xyz123
Chris Oncall: BMC reports node powered off -> on. Rebooted at 3849998950. Boot logs show driver reloaded; waiting for node to rejoin k8s.
Jordan Ops: node back and ready but kubelet notice of new GPU hw_id different. Running full hw sanity.
Rita SRE: running memtest + nvcheck now. If tests pass, we'll run a controlled canary with 2 pods and monitor for 10m. If any Xid reappears, node will be quarantined for replacement.
Tom Eng-runtime: FYI — we already routed critical traffic to other AZ capacity, no major SLO breaches expected. Still tracking errors for customers.
Lina Support: updating customers: initial mitigation applied (fallback + routing). Next update in 15m. :thumbsup:
customer-bridge-bot: Bridge notes appended. Next oncall rotation in 2h will take postmortem. @Rita SRE please lead the write-up.
Rita SRE: will do. Adding runbook links and commands used to the incident doc. Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/evacuate-gpu-node
Maya MLOps: PR merged for smaller batch fallback. Rolling out now.
Tom Eng-runtime: monitoring — ECC counts dropping post-reboot but still non-zero. Will keep the alert on.
Rita SRE: handing off to night oncall. @Chris Oncall will keep watch and coordinate with hardware replacement if Xid recurs. Moving to monitoring->postmortem flow.
Chris Oncall: acknowledged. I'll continue to watch the bridge and escalate to infra if we see any repeat.
Lina Support: final note for now: customers notified, bridge open, replacements requested.
Rita SRE: thanks team. Closing active paging loop; incident retained for postmortem. :white_check_mark:
